senses.definition: To have a consequence or remnant.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To cause or allow (something) to remain as available; to refrain from taking (something) away; to stop short of consuming or otherwise depleting (something) entirely.
examples: I left my car at home and took a bus to work.
The ants did not leave so much as a crumb of bread.
There's not much food left. We'd better go to the shops.

quotes.text: […] St. Bede's at this period of its history was perhaps the poorest and most miserable parish in the East End of London. quotes.text: Plant breeding is always a numbers game.[…]. The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation,[…]. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better. These rarities may be new mutations, or they can be existing ones that are neutral—or are even selected against—in a wild population. A good example is mutations that disrupt seed dispersal, leaving the seeds on the heads long after they are ripe.

subsenses.definition: (transitive or intransitive, copulative) To cause, to result in.
examples: The lightning left her dazzled for several minutes.
Infantile paralysis left him lame for the rest of his life.
She left disappointed.
The accident left the car a heap of twisted metal.

examples: Leave your hat in the hall.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To let be or do without interference.
examples: I left him to his reflections.
I leave my hearers to judge.
I'll leave it to you to decide.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To depart from; to end one's connection or affiliation with.
(transitive) To end one's membership in (a group); to terminate one's affiliation with (an organization); to stop participating in (a project).
examples:
2018, The Independent, "Brexit: Theresa May 'not bluffing' in threat to leave EU without a deal, Tory minister Liam Fox says"

subsenses.definition: (euphemistic, transitive) To die (the object denotes those affected by the death).

quotes.text: The other evening Sheri called to tell me that Connie had left us, and that I will never again be able to hold my pot luck supper plate on my knee and listen to Connie's wonderful talk or see her slow, almost impish smile.

subsenses.definition: (intransitive) To depart; to go away from a certain place or state.
examples: I think you'd better leave.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To transfer possession of after death.
examples: When my father died, he left me the house.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To give (something) to someone; to deliver (something) to a repository; to deposit.
examples: I'll leave the car in the station so you can pick it up there.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To transfer responsibility or attention of (something) (to someone); to stop being concerned with.
examples: Can't we just leave this to the experts?
